A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the use of the transformation of the over-dispersed count data to continuous data is an effective way to analyze bivariate clustered data with a continuous and over-dispersed discrete outcome.
the multilevel model is a useful tool in analyzing clustered data and that the transformation method can be used in the presence of over-dispersion.
the use of the transformation method is recommended when dealing with bivariate data where one outcome is continuous, and one outcome is over-dispersed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a random effects model to analyze bivariate outcomes is only appropriate if the data has been appropriately transformed.
the multilevel models can yield misleading results if the data are not transformed.
the use of a simple transformation of the data can yield accurate results for bivariate outcomes with one continuous and one over-dispersed count response variable.
